decisionRule: Routine nursing assessment, documentation, physician/family coordination and reasonable short-term enhanced monitoring remain part of the resident's LOC nursing oversight.
examples: Extra vital signs, bleeding observation after medication change, short-term symptom checks.
reassessmentSafeguard: If intensity/duration becomes material or recurrent, reassess LOC/modifier/service.

includedInLoc: No, unless specifically bundled in package
decisionRule: A procedure requiring licensed nursing skill, material nursing time or special competency may be separately charged when outside the defined LOC inclusion.
examples: IM/SC injection, catheter insertion/change, selected complex procedures.
requiredDocumentation: Order/clinical indication; procedure record; staff qualification; fee disclosure.
reassessmentSafeguard: Do not separately charge if explicitly included in resident's package.

service: IV therapy / IV hydration / IV medication
decisionRule: IV therapy is an additional skilled service and must also pass LifeCare capability/scope criteria.
requiredDocumentation: Physician order; consent as applicable; supplies; monitoring; capability approval.

decisionRule: Low-complexity, limited-frequency wound care may be bundled by LOC/package; charge separately only when outside the published inclusion.
examples: Example: simple dressing at limited frequency vs recurring skilled wound treatment.
requiredDocumentation: Wound assessment; order; frequency; supplies; package comparison.

decisionRule: Complex, high-frequency or resource-intensive wound care is an additional skilled nursing service.
examples: Complex dressing regimen, frequent treatment, specialized materials.
requiredDocumentation: Wound plan; frequency; procedure time; materials; progress review.
reassessmentSafeguard: Do not let recurring wound charges continue indefinitely without care-model reassessment.

decisionRule: Routine medication administration/support already included in the resident's approved package is not separately charged.
reassessmentSafeguard: Medication complexity may modify LOC/care package but should not create duplicate fees.

decisionRule: A prescribed short course of injections may be charged per procedure/service schedule.
requiredDocumentation: Order; administration record; drug/supply source; duration.
reassessmentSafeguard: End charge when course ends; reassess if it becomes chronic.

decisionRule: When a temporary procedure becomes a stable recurring need, determine whether it belongs in LOC/package, a recurring clinical add-on, or exceeds capability.
examples: Daily long-term injections, recurring specialized treatment.
requiredDocumentation: Utilization history; clinical need; LOC comparison; pricing approval.
reassessmentSafeguard: Mandatory periodic review; avoid perpetual 'temporary' billing.

decisionRule: Resident-specific consumables/equipment outside standard inclusions may be charged separately with transparent pricing.
examples: Special wound materials, IV supplies, external equipment rental.
requiredDocumentation: Item/service record; source cost/fee; family disclosure.
reassessmentSafeguard: Avoid markup ambiguity; define standard included supplies.

decisionRule: Dedicated licensed nursing time is distinct from shared LOC nursing oversight and from a private caregiver.
requiredDocumentation: Clinical rationale; hours; nursing scope; authorization; review date.
reassessmentSafeguard: Use only when within capability and clinically justified.

decisionRule: External physician, therapist, laboratory, diagnostic or specialist services are outside the core LOC unless contractually included.
requiredDocumentation: Referral/order; provider; family authorization; invoice arrangement.
reassessmentSafeguard: Clarify LifeCare coordination fee, if any, separately.

decisionRule: Transport and dedicated escort outside routine community services may be separately charged.
requiredDocumentation: Trip/escort record; duration; destination; fee basis.

separateCharge: Do not solve by fee alone
decisionRule: Additional charges cannot be used to retain a resident whose condition requires services beyond LifeCare's safe capability.
Before any additional clinical fee, verify that the same intervention/time/material is not already included in LOC, PCG, dedicated nursing or another billed package.
examples: Cross-check service against package inclusions and other active add-ons.
reassessmentSafeguard: No duplicate billing for the same unit of service.

decisionRule: A temporary additional service that persists beyond the defined course/review period must trigger reassessment rather than automatic continued billing.
examples: Repeated wound care, injections, intensive monitoring.
requiredDocumentation: Start date; utilization/frequency; review date; reassessment outcome.
reassessmentSafeguard: Set service-specific review periods in policy/fee schedule.
